symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The fixed finite horizon \(H\ge 1\).

symbols.name: Tset
symbols.def: The decision-stage set \(\mathcal T=\{1,\ldots,H\}\).

symbols.name: Sset
symbols.def: The finite state alphabet.

symbols.name: Aset
symbols.def: The finite action alphabet.

symbols.name: Rset
symbols.def: The finite reward alphabet.

symbols.name: Mset
symbols.def: The reward-recording indicator alphabet.

symbols.name: Hfull
symbols.def: For \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(\mathcal H_t^F\) contains \(H_t^F=(S_1,A_1,R_1,M_1,\ldots,S_t)\), with all past rewards retained even when missing in the record.

symbols.name: Hobs
symbols.def: For \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(\mathcal H_t^O\) contains \(H_t^O=(S_1,A_1,M_1,M_1R_1,\ldots,S_t)\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: The set of complete trajectories \(\omega=(S_1,A_1,R_1,M_1,S_2,\ldots,A_H,R_H,M_H,S_{H+1})\).

symbols.name: Ospace
symbols.def: The set of recorded trajectories obtained by replacing each \(R_t\) with \((M_t,M_tR_t)\).

symbols.name: Omap
symbols.def: The deterministic coarsening map that erases \(R_t\) whenever \(M_t=0\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: The observed trajectory law.

symbols.name: Xsa
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X_{SA}(p)=\{(s,a)\in\mathcal S\times\mathcal A:p(S_1=s,A_1=a)>0\}\), the positive-mass baseline-state/action cells used by the static reduction.

symbols.name: Achen
symbols.def: For \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\), \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\); this is the observed respondent shadow-by-reward table.

symbols.name: betachen
symbols.def: For \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\), \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\); this is the observed nonrespondent shadow vector.

symbols.name: Wchen
symbols.def: \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\), the feasible nonresponse-odds vectors in a positive-mass static cell.

symbols.name: Jchen
symbols.def: \(\mathcal J_{s,a}=\{\mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}\operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w+\mathbf 1):w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\}\), the Chen conditional-mean program for cell \((s,a)\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: A candidate complete trajectory law under the behavior policy.

symbols.name: qcell
symbols.def: The cylinder marginal of \(q\) at \((H_t^F,A_t,R_t,M_t,S_{t+1})=(h,a,r,m,s')\).

symbols.name: qobs
symbols.def: The cylinder marginal of \(q\) at \((H_t^O,A_t)=(g,a)\), with \(q_t^O(g)=\sum_a q_t^O(g,a)\).

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: The known behavior policy based on recorded history.

symbols.name: pi
symbols.def: The fixed oracle complete-information deployment policy, allowed to depend on latent reward history; operational implementation requires a separately supplied reward-recovery or sensing mechanism.

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.def: A behavior-policy overlap constant.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho_t^\pi(\omega)=\prod_{u=1}^t \pi_u(A_u\mid H_u^F)/\mu_u(A_u\mid H_u^O)\).

symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: \(\ell_t(q)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)\rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)\).

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V_\pi(q)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t(q)\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: The full-history compatible-law fiber defined in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\).

symbols.name: Theta
symbols.def: The sharp policy-value image defined in \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The attained lower endpoint of \(\Theta_I(p)\).

symbols.name: U
symbols.def: The attained upper endpoint of \(\Theta_I(p)\).

symbols.name: It
symbols.def: The stagewise continuation-weighted Chen projection defined in \(\mathrm{def{:}stagewise\text{-}projection}\).

symbols.name: lt
symbols.def: \(\ell_t^-(p)=\min I_t(p)\).

symbols.name: ut
symbols.def: \(\ell_t^+(p)=\max I_t(p)\).

symbols.name: Thetarect
symbols.def: The Minkowski sum of the stagewise value projections \(I_t(p)\).

symbols.name: Lrect
symbols.def: \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t^-(p)\).

symbols.name: Urect
symbols.def: \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t^+(p)\).

symbols.name: Fminus
symbols.def: \(F_t^-(p)=\{q\in\mathcal K(p):\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^-(p)\}\).

symbols.name: Fplus
symbols.def: \(F_t^+(p)=\{q\in\mathcal K(p):\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^+(p)\}\).

symbols.name: Fjointminus
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak F^-(p)=\bigcap_{t\in\mathcal T}F_t^-(p)\).

symbols.name: Fjointplus
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak F^+(p)=\bigcap_{t\in\mathcal T}F_t^+(p)\).

symbols.name: DeltaMinus
symbols.def: \(\Delta^-(p)=L(p)-L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\).

symbols.name: DeltaPlus
symbols.def: \(\Delta^+(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)-U(p)\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independent recorded trajectories.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: The confidence error probability.

symbols.name: Osample
symbols.def: The recorded trajectory sample.

symbols.name: phat
symbols.def: \(\widehat p_n(o)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{O_i=o\}\).

symbols.name: calpha
symbols.def: The smallest \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(2nD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat p_n\Vert p')\) under \(n\widehat p_n\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(n,p')\), with \(0\log 0=0\).

symbols.name: Cfiber
symbols.def: The simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber defined in \(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\text{-}fiber}\).

symbols.name: Thetahat
symbols.def: The unrestricted union of sharp policy-value images over \(C_{n,\alpha}\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: A requested global-optimization tolerance.

symbols.name: Nvar
symbols.def: The number of real variables in the fixed-law compatible-fiber value formula, including latent probabilities and the scalar value coordinate.

symbols.name: scon
symbols.def: The number of polynomial equalities and weak inequalities in the fixed-law compatible-fiber value formula.

symbols.name: dmax
symbols.def: The maximum total degree of those polynomials.

symbols.name: Bcert
symbols.def: A cylindrical algebraic decomposition procedure for the fixed-law formula \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\) and \(v=V_\pi(q)\), returning an exact univariate description or certified \(\eta\)-enclosures.

symbols.name: Ytwo
symbols.def: The recorded reward code in the exact two-stage submodel, with \(Y_t=0\) whenever \(M_t=0\).

symbols.name: Xtwo
symbols.def: The full recorded-trajectory atom array for the exact two-stage submodel.

symbols.name: Qtwo
symbols.def: The complete-trajectory atom array corresponding to the observed array \(x\) in the exact two-stage submodel.

symbols.name: Lambdatwo
symbols.def: The free coordinates remaining after exact row reduction of the two-stage observed-marginal and behavior equations.

symbols.name: Qzerotwo
symbols.def: The affine offset produced by exact row reduction of the two-stage linear constraints.

symbols.name: Btwo
symbols.def: The null-space matrix produced by exact row reduction, so the linear completion coordinates are \(q=q^0(x,\mu)+B(\mu)\lambda\).

symbols.name: Dtwo
symbols.def: A \(2\times2\) minor of a two-row, three-reward respondent shadow block.

symbols.name: Ztwo
symbols.def: The signed-minor null vector of a two-row, three-reward respondent shadow block.

symbols.name: Ctwo
symbols.def: The three reward-coordinate coefficients obtained after substituting the exact two-stage behavior and oracle-policy weights into a continuation-value objective.

symbols.name: Gtwo
symbols.def: The determinant formed by appending a continuation-coefficient row to a two-row respondent shadow block.

symbols.name: Mtwo
symbols.def: The coefficient-expanded elimination polynomials obtained from the two-stage cross-products, feasibility boundaries, and opposite stage-face optimality systems.

symbols.name: Rstrict
symbols.def: The compatible observed-law, behavior-policy, and oracle-policy triples satisfying the printed strict sign vector for the polynomials \(M_j\).

symbols.name: Jeq
symbols.def: The printed subfamily of elimination-polynomial indices defining the exceptional equality locus.

symbols.name: Eeq
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal V(M_j:j\in\mathcal J_{\mathrm{eq}})\), intersected with the compatible two-stage parameter space.

assumptions.condition: \(q_t^O(g,a)=\mu_t(a\mid g)\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^O(g,a')\quad\forall t\in\mathcal T,\ g\in\mathcal H_t^O,\ a\in\mathcal A\).
\(\mu_t(a\mid g)\ge\epsilon\quad\forall t\in\mathcal T,\ g\in\mathcal H_t^O,\ a\in\mathcal A\).

\(S_{t+1}\perp M_t\mid(H_t^F,A_t,R_t)\) for every \(t\in\mathcal T\); on all cells, including zero-mass conditioning cells, this means the polynomial equations \(q_t(h,a,r,1,s)q_t(h,a,r,0,s')=q_t(h,a,r,0,s)q_t(h,a,r,1,s')\) for every \(h\in\mathcal H_t^F\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(r\in\mathcal R\), and \(s,s'\in\mathcal S\).

novel.justification: A temporal structural causal model satisfies the restriction when, conditional on the complete latent past, current action, and current reward, the recording mechanism and next-state innovation have independent disturbances and recording has no causal effect on the next state. This describes delayed administrative recording or passive sensor dropout that does not alter care after conditioning on the complete clinical history.

standard.name: Correct specification of the compatibility model

definitions.name: Full-history weak-shadow compatible-law fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal K(p)=\{q\in\Delta(\Omega): O_\#q=p;\ q_t^O(g,a)=\mu_t(a\mid g)\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^O(g,a')\ \forall(t,g,a)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal H_t^O\times\mathcal A;\ q_t(h,a,r,1,s)q_t(h,a,r,0,s')=q_t(h,a,r,0,s)q_t(h,a,r,1,s')\ \forall(t,h,a,r,s,s')\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal H_t^F\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal R\times\mathcal S^2\}\).

definitions.name: Observed-cell Chen program for the one-stage reduction
definitions.construction: For \(H=1\), \(S_2\) plays the role of Chen's always-observed \(F\). For each \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\), set \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\). Then \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\) and \(\mathcal J_{s,a}=\{\mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}\operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w+\mathbf 1):w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\}\).

definitions.name: Correctly continuation-weighted stagewise Chen projection
definitions.construction: For every \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(I_t(p)=\{\ell_t(q):q\in\mathcal K(p)\}\), \(\ell_t^-(p)=\min I_t(p)\), and \(\ell_t^+(p)=\max I_t(p)\).

definitions.name: Product-of-projections value relaxation
definitions.construction: \(\Theta^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\{\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}x_t:x_t\in I_t(p)\}\), with endpoint pair \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t^-(p)\) and \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t^+(p)\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous extremizing-face systems
definitions.construction: For \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\), \(F_t^-(p)=\{q\in\mathcal K(p):\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^-(p)\}\), \(F_t^+(p)=\{q\in\mathcal K(p):\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^+(p)\}\), and \(\mathfrak F^\sigma(p)=\bigcap_{t\in\mathcal T}F_t^\sigma(p)\).

definitions.name: Exact simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber
definitions.construction: \(C_{n,\alpha}=\{p'\in\Delta(\mathcal O):2nD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat p_n\Vert p')\le c_{n,\alpha}(p')\}\), where \(c_{n,\alpha}(p')\) is the smallest \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile under \(n\widehat p_n\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(n,p')\) and the conventions are \(0\log(0/x)=0\) and \(x\log(x/0)=+\infty\) for \(x>0\).

definitions.name: Fixed-law certified value-image elimination
definitions.construction: For fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\), apply \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) to the first-order real formula \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\); isolate every real boundary root exactly, or stop root isolation after disjoint rational intervals of width at most \(\eta\) have been certified.

definitions.name: Exact two-stage elimination dossier handle
definitions.construction: Handle: fix \(H=2\), \(S_1=s_0\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\), and write \(Y_t=M_tR_t\). Enumerate the observed table coefficient by coefficient as \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}=p(A_1=a_1,M_1=m_1,Y_1=y_1,S_2=s_2,A_2=a_2,M_2=m_2,Y_2=y_2,S_3=s_3)\), where \(y_t=0\) if \(m_t=0\) and \(y_t\in\mathcal R\) if \(m_t=1\). Enumerate the complete table as \(q_{a_1r_1m_1s_2a_2r_2m_2s_3}\), impose \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}=\sum_{r_1:m_1r_1=y_1}\sum_{r_2:m_2r_2=y_2}q_{a_1r_1m_1s_2a_2r_2m_2s_3}\) together with the known behavior equations, and perform exact rational row reduction to \(q=q^0(x,\mu)+B(\mu)\lambda\). Substitute this parameterization into every weak-shadow cross-product. For each observable \(2\times3\) respondent shadow block \(A\), define \(D^{ij}=A_{0i}A_{1j}-A_{0j}A_{1i}\) and \(z=(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})\); append the continuation-value coefficient row \(c(x,\mu,\pi)\) to form \(G=\det[(A_{0\cdot});(A_{1\cdot});c^\top]\). Eliminate \(\lambda\) from the cross-products, feasibility boundaries, and the two pairs of opposite stage-face optimality systems by a lexicographic Gröbner basis or resultants. The output must be a coefficient-expanded finite list \(M_j(x,\mu,\pi)\), a declared sign vector, and the corresponding common-zero ideal; names such as ``the relevant minors'' without the displayed coefficients do not complete the obligation.

statements.statement: For every \(p\) satisfying \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), the fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\Delta(\Omega)\), the image \(\Theta_I(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\), and there exist \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) with \(V_\pi(q^-)=L(p)\) and \(V_\pi(q^+)=U(p)\). Every reported endpoint is therefore attained by a full trajectory law reproducing the observed cells, the known behavior factors, and all weak-shadow cross-product equations.
statements.justification: Attainment upgrades a numerical outer range into sharp policy-value endpoints supported by compatible data-generating laws.
statements.gap: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\), establish static cellwise sharp bounds; the present compact fiber is dynamically coupled and generally nonconvex because full-history exclusion is imposed by cross-products.
statements.consumer: Clinical OPE analysts can report certified worst- and best-case deployment values without interpreting local-solver output as sharp.

statements.statement: Supporting compact-face lemma. For every nonempty compact fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\), \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\le L(p)\le U(p)\le U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\). Moreover, \(L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) if and only if \(\mathfrak F^-(p)\ne\varnothing\), and \(U(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) if and only if \(\mathfrak F^+(p)\ne\varnothing\). Empty common minimizing or maximizing faces therefore imply, respectively, \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\).
statements.justification: This compact-set identity supplies the geometric criterion used by the strict-containment obligation; it is supporting machinery, not a headline result.
statements.gap: The identity is an elementary min-of-a-sum fact on a compact set, so no field-level novelty is claimed.
statements.consumer: The exact two-stage analysis can certify strict containment by proving that one of the two common-face intersections is empty.

statements.statement: Sanity Corollary (one-stage Chen reduction). Let \(H=1\), so that \(S_2\) plays Chen's always-observed \(F\) role. For every \(s\) with \(p(S_1=s)>0\) and every \(a\in\mathcal A\), behavior positivity implies \(p(S_1=s,A_1=a)>0\). In each such cell define the observed respondent matrix and nonrespondent vector from the observed reward, response, and shadow table by \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\). Suppose cellwise response positivity holds: \(\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}A_{s,a}[s',r]>0\) for every \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\). Then the global fiber decomposes cellwise as \(\mathcal K(p)\cong\prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}\), where \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\), and its value image is \(\Theta_I(p)=\{\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}:\theta_{s,a}\in\mathcal J_{s,a}\}\). Hence the endpoints are the corresponding weighted sums of the Chen cell-program endpoints. If every positive-mass cell matrix satisfies the precise full-column-rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\), necessarily with \(|\mathcal S|\ge|\mathcal R|\), then feasibility makes every \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) a singleton and the one-stage value is point identified. This is the cell program of Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\).
statements.justification: The one-stage decomposition is a non-novel sanity corollary pinned to Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\).
statements.gap: The cited proposition already gives the static sharp interval and full-column-rank point-identification result; the corollary only verifies that the dynamic notation reduces cell by cell under explicit response positivity.
statements.consumer: Existing static weak-shadow software becomes a regression test for the dynamic implementation.

statements.statement: Sole headline open obligation (exact two-stage generic strict containment). Execute \(\mathrm{def{:}strictness\text{-}handle}\) on the model \(H=2\), \(S_1=s_0\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\). The deliverable is one coefficient-complete algebraic dossier satisfying all of the following requirements: (i) list every rational observed atom \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}\), every rational behavior and oracle-policy probability, the complete affine parameterization \(q=q^0+B\lambda\), and every feasible interval or semialgebraic constraint on \(\lambda\); (ii) display every \(D^{ij}\), every continuation determinant \(G\), every elimination polynomial \(M_j(x,\mu,\pi)\), and one explicit strict sign vector; (iii) prove that the compatible sign region \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{strict}}=\{(x,\mu,\pi):M_j\mathrel{\triangleright_j}0\ \text{ for every listed }j\}\) is nonempty and relatively open, with each relation \(\triangleright_j\in\{>,<,\ne\}\) printed in the dossier; (iv) prove on all of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{strict}}\) that \(\pi_2(\cdot\mid r_1)\) differs for at least two latent rewards and that \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\); (v) give one cell-by-cell exact rational witness, verify normalization, observed marginalization, known behavior factors, positivity, all weak-shadow cross-products, \(A w=\boldsymbol\beta\), the null directions, and certify \(\Theta_I(p)=[229/140,26/15]\) together with exact rational \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) and \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) establishing a strict endpoint gap; and (vi) prove that, away from explicitly listed rank-degenerate and reward-history-blind policy faces, the equality locus is exactly the compatible part of the coefficient-expanded common-zero variety \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal V(M_j:j\in J_{\mathrm{eq}})\), with the index set \(J_{\mathrm{eq}}\) printed. Until this dossier is supplied, generic strict containment is an open question and no existence of the table, sign region, or equality characterization is asserted. Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, obtains Bellman recursion after assuming rectangular ambiguity; this obligation must instead establish strict nonrectangularity of an inverse observed-data fiber.
statements.justification: A coefficient-complete relatively open strictness region, not the compact-face identity, is the sole theorem-level novelty target.
statements.gap: Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, assumes a rectangular product of conditional ambiguity sets to obtain robust recursion. Static weak-shadow programs do not determine whether the dynamically coupled inverse observed-data fiber is strictly nonrectangular.
statements.consumer: The printed sign certificate would let a sepsis OPE analyst detect when stagewise MNAR bounds are provably too wide for an oracle policy that reacts to latent reward history.

statements.statement: For finite alphabets and fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\) with \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) terminates on \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\) and returns all connected components of \(\Theta_I(p)\) as closed intervals or singleton points with exact real-algebraic endpoints; alternatively it returns disjoint certified rational \(\eta\)-enclosures of every component and endpoint. For a presentation with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\), classical sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition uses at most \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\) arithmetic operations, with exact coefficient arithmetic, and the same bound controls the number of cells examined.
statements.justification: The result turns fixed-law sharpness into a terminating exact computation rather than a local numerical optimization claim.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. (2024) motivate certified polynomial optimization for discrete causal models; this theorem specializes exact real elimination to the coupled weak-shadow value image and reports all connected components.
statements.consumer: An auditor can reproduce exact algebraic policy-value bounds for a finite sepsis table or request certified enclosures at tolerance \(\eta\).

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling of complete recorded trajectories from a finite-horizon behavior process.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent trajectories with one multinomial cell in \(\mathcal O\) per trajectory.
sampling_model.treatment: Actions are generated by the known recorded-history behavior policy \(\mu\). The fixed deployment rule \(\pi\) is an oracle complete-information policy when it uses latent rewards; deployment requires a separately supplied reward-recovery or sensing mechanism.
sampling_model.overlap: \(\mu_t(a\mid H_t^O)\ge\epsilon>0\) on every finite history-action cell.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The observed multinomial law is inverted jointly for validity. Fixed-law value images are computed by exact real quantifier elimination over latent trajectory probabilities; the KL confidence fiber is not represented as a polynomial program.

tldr: Finite-horizon off-policy value with MNAR discrete rewards is the image of a compact semialgebraic full-history fiber. The sole headline target is an exact \(H=2\), binary-action, three-reward generic strict-containment result: a coefficient-complete observed table, rational completion parameterization, observable elimination minors with a nonempty relatively open sign region, an exact witness, and the exceptional equality variety. A compact common-face lemma is supporting geometry, and the one-stage Chen reduction is a non-novel sanity proposition anchored only by the source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\). Sharp endpoint attainment and fixed-law exact elimination remain supporting results.

Iyengar's rectangular robust dynamic program assumes the product structure that an MNAR observed-data inverse fiber need not possess.

project_justification.fill: The project makes that exact two-stage generic strict-containment dossier the sole headline obligation. Compact attainment, common-face geometry, the source-label-pinned one-stage Chen sanity reduction, and fixed-law quantifier elimination serve only as supporting results.

It requires a fully enumerated rational observed table and completion map, coefficient-expanded observable minors with printed signs, a certified nonempty relatively open region, a cell-by-cell rational witness with a strict endpoint gap, and an exact exceptional equality variety. Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, assumes rectangular ambiguity to obtain robust recursion, while the open obligation must prove strict nonrectangularity of an inverse observed-data fiber.
